nh_05_east_face_upper.blurb: The upper band of Mt. Willard's east face, above Crawford Notch, is a winter-only venue with 17 climbs, nearly all of them frozen lines. Expect moderate to solid water ice, with most routes between WI3 and WI4, a couple of WI5s and one WI6, plus two mixed lines (roughly M6 and M10) and a single rock-and-ice route. Several lines run two pitches, and the face holds enough to fill a full day. It is a cold, exposed spot with an alpine feel, even though the cliff is not a true high-mountain wall. Top out through one of the gullies and a climbers' trail leads to the Mt. Willard Trail for the walk back down.

nh_swirley_boulder.blurb: A house-sized boulder in the Blair Woods section of Pawtuckaway State Park, Nottingham, and the headline piece of that wooded area. It carries 17 problems on every side, running from an easy slab around V1 up to a handful of very hard lines in the V11 to V13 range, with a good number in the V7 to V9 band. The rock is steep on all faces and the boulder sits in a cool, damp hollow, so dry conditions matter. The surrounding woods are quiet and a short walk from the lot. Come with a solid pad setup and a spotter or two, since many lines are tall and committing.

nh_monsters_from_the_id.blurb: A steep, powerful sport crag at Rumney, with 17 routes that are almost all bolted and one trad line. The grades start around 5.10 and then jump straight into the hard stuff: a handful at 5.11, a couple at 5.12, and the majority at 5.13 and 5.14, so this is a place for strong climbers. The wall faces south and warms up quickly in sun, which makes it a good pick on a cold winter day, and it stays shaded for a while on summer mornings. Spring seepage can put many lines out of play. Reach it by a short scramble through boulders or a hillside trail.

nh_milestones_the.blurb: A small bouldering spot in Pawtuckaway State Park made up of three medium-sized boulders lined up one after another, with 16 problems in total. It suits a mixed group: several easy and moderate lines from VB through V1 and V3 to V4, with a few harder ones and a top end around V10. The walk in is under a mile of mostly flat trail past the Round Pond boulders and across the pond inlet, so it feels removed from the busier blocs. The boulders can be a bit dirty, so bring a brush. Autumn is the best season in the park, as bugs fade and the weather cools.

nh_rand_mountain.blurb: A hilltop cliff in New Durham, on the east side of Lake Winnipesaukee, standing roughly 30 to 70 feet tall with boulders scattered at its base. Of its 17 routes, 15 are traditional, with one sport line and one top-rope. Grades span a whole range: a very easy chimney, a few climbs in the 5.6 to 5.7 zone, a solid cluster at 5.9 to 5.10, and a few harder lines up to 5.13. A dike feature on the face shows up in some route names. The crag requires a woodland hike of about half an hour and tends to feel secluded.
